Theme

Money, work & business

expense noun

also expenses, expenditure, outlay, costs, at my expense, at someone’s expense, go to expense, spare no expense, cost, at your own expense

classical

Cic. Att. 5.14.2: adventus noster nēminī nē minimō quidem fuit sūmptuī
Caes. BG 1.18.5: suō sūmptū, at his own expense
Traupman 311: meō sūmptū, at my expense
Traupman 311

sūmptus, sūmptūs m.

noun, fourth declension · Declension on Wiktionary

expense, cost, outlay

The everyday word, in the singular or the plural (Lewis & Short). At my expense, meō sūmptū; to go to expense, sūmptum facere; to spare no expense, sūmptū nōn parcere (Cic. Fam. 16.4.2, see spend). To be a cost to someone is sūmptuī esse alicui.

Other words

  • impēnsa, impēnsae f. — outlay, cost (money laid out on something)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 13.25.3: quoniam impēnsam fēcimus in macrocola (Lewis & Short); Sen. Ep. 12.1: dē impēnsīs aedificiī; Traupman 311; Traupman 130; Traupman 297 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Properly money laid out (pecūnia understood, from impendere, to spend): impēnsam facere in rem, to spend money on a thing.

  • impendium, impendiī n. — outlay, cost

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Quinct. 12: sine impendiō (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Mostly in the plural (Lewis & Short). In Cicero’s letters it is also the interest paid on a loan (faenus et impendium, Att. 6.1.4), so say sūmptus where that could mislead.

Examples

  • nūllus sūmptus est, et sī sūmptus esset, tamen valētūdinis causā experīrēs

    it costs nothing, and even if there were an expense, you would still try it for your healthCato Agr. 157

  • adventus noster nēminī nē minimō quidem fuit sūmptuī

    my arrival did not cost anyone a pennyCic. Att. 5.14.2

  • vēneram in suburbānum meum et querēbar dē impēnsīs aedificiī dīlābentis

    I had come out to my place outside town and was complaining about the cost of the crumbling buildingSen. Ep. 12.1

  • prīvātō sūmptū

    at one’s own expenseTraupman 311

See also spend, budget, cost a lot, price, income, finance.
